title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign a 97.1% probability to no U.S. debt default by the end of 2027 because Congress has consistently raised or suspended the debt limit ahead of any X-date, most recently via the 2025 reconciliation bill that set the ceiling at $41.1 trillion. With gross federal debt now at approximately $40 trillion, projections place the next limit breach in mid-2027, followed by six to nine months of extraordinary measures that would push any potential shortfall into 2028. Strong ongoing demand for Treasuries, the dollar’s reserve-currency status, and broad recognition that even brief nonpayment would raise borrowing costs and disrupt markets reinforce this consensus. A narrow window for change before December 2026 remains tied to the timing and outcome of 2027 debt-ceiling negotiations.
